title: 3Sum
prompt:
Given an integer array `nums`, return all **unique** triplets `[a, b, c]` with `a + b + c == 0`. No duplicate triplets in the output (order within/among triplets doesn't matter).

**Example**: `[-1,0,1,2,-1,-4]` → `[[-1,-1,2],[-1,0,1]]`.

The classic composition: sort, fix the first element, then run Two Sum II's two pointers on the rest — with careful duplicate-skipping.
hints: Sort first. For each index i, solve Two Sum on nums[i+1..] targeting -nums[i].
Skip duplicate anchors: `if (i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i - 1]) continue;`
After recording a triplet, advance l past equal values (`while (l < r && nums[l] == nums[l + 1]) l++;`) before the normal l++.

solution.explanation: O(n²): n anchors × O(n) two-pointer sweep. The three duplicate-skips (anchor, second element, plus the natural r--) are what guarantee uniqueness without a Set. The `nums[i] > 0` break is a free optimization on sorted data.
